checkpoints.notes: 5 candidates (4 evolutions + 1 fresh, per user direction). Selected Drift Maze: Deep Drift (seeded procedural generation, exact solver, real breakable-wall mechanic, par/undo/hint). Code review found breakable walls were functionally floor, campaign pars 1-6, par never displayed.
Cracked walls stop-and-shatter; exact BFS over (position, shattered-wall mask); seeded generate-and-test generator with 4 tiers; endless mode, computed par, undo, hint.
Playable locally by opening game/drift-maze.html; endless mode via M or ?mode=endless&seed=N.
All suites pass: 20/20 rule+solver checks, 10/10 campaign levels, 600 generated levels (median par by tier 6<7<9<12, all in band), 20/20 browser assertions.

followUps: Human playtest of the endless tiers: par length is the only difficulty measure so far.
Campaign levels 7 and 8 are 1- and 2-move levels; rework or replace them with curated generated levels.

Orbit Duel: Rival AI already exists on unmerged branches claude/magical-turing-jfrd8s and claude/magical-turing-560d4n; merge one instead of rebuilding. Note those branches moved files differently (check paths before merging).
Orbit Duel: Gauntlet (solo wave mode) is the runner-up concept, best attempted after a human playtest of Orbit Duel's feel.
budgetNotes: Single session, no subagent fan-out; research and design done inline rather than on separate models to conserve budget.
resumeInstructions: Cycle 3 (Drift Maze: Deep Drift) is complete with valid outputs at every checkpoint; do not re-execute it. Next run starts Cycle 4 at 'research'. User direction (2026-09-19) still applies: bias candidates toward deepening Orbit Duel and Drift Maze. Read docs/cycle1-concepts.md, docs/cycle2-concepts.md and docs/cycle3-concepts.md for prior art. branchNote: IMPORTANT: every scheduled run starts from the repo default branch and pushes to a new claude/* branch. Unless that branch is merged into the default branch, the next run reads stale state. As of 2026-11-11 there were 35 unmerged branches that each redid 'Cycle 2'. This cycle was built on top of claude/magical-turing-nlpcnj.

checkpoints.notes: 5 concepts brainstormed and scored; Orbit Duel selected, Gravity Flip Runner as fallback.
Single-file HTML5 canvas architecture, tunable constants, testing plan defined.
Self-contained playable prototype: 2-player local gravity-duel arcade game, no build step, no external assets/deps.

Automated Playwright/headless-Chromium smoke tests: load+interaction test and ~6s extended-session test, both PASS. Found and fixed one test-hook staleness bug (window.__orbitDuel.bullets snapshot vs live getter) during testing. Win-condition end-to-end and fun/balance tuning are NOT covered by automated tests -- flagged as follow-up.

followUps: Human/manual playtest of Orbit Duel for feel/balance tuning (SHIP_THRUST, SHIP_DRAG, G, BULLET_SPEED).
Automated end-to-end test of the win condition + restart flow.
Consider a simple AI opponent or additional modes if this concept is revisited in a future cycle.
history.budgetNotes: Single-session run, no subagent fan-out used to conserve budget. Implementation kept to one self-contained HTML file (no build step) to keep scope tight. Cycle 1 completed fully within budget with no usage-limit warning encountered.

checkpoints.notes: 5 concepts brainstormed and scored (incl. an Orbit Duel AI-opponent evolution as a low-novelty baseline); Drift Maze (ice-slide grid puzzle) selected for full determinism / scriptable testability with no human playtester in the loop. Tidal Push was runner-up on novelty but higher edge-case risk.

Turn-based grid architecture in a single self-contained game/drift-maze.html; pure slide() grid engine decoupled from rendering to enable BFS solvability checks + rule unit tests + an automated win-condition end-to-end test (addressing Cycle 1's biggest testing gap). 10-level hand-authored plan, escalating tile mechanics (walls -> breakable walls -> one-way gates -> teleport pads).

Pure grid-logic module + 10 hand-authored levels + canvas renderer/input, plus three reusable automated-test scripts (BFS solvability/mechanic-necessity checker, slide() rule unit tests, Playwright browser+win-condition e2e test).

All automated checks pass: 10/10 levels solvable with required mechanics confirmed non-bypassable, 12/12 slide() rule unit tests, 8/8 browser assertions including a scripted win-condition end-to-end test (using the solver's own optimal path) that directly closes the Cycle 1 follow-up Orbit Duel couldn't cover. Found and fixed a teleport-pairing logic bug (searched for the same pad char instead of its pair) and a Level 10 pillar/gate column misalignment during testing; also caught and fixed a design-level bug pre-test where most levels' special tiles were bypassable via a trivial 'right,down' shortcut.

followUps: Human playtest of the difficulty curve across the 10 levels (the solver confirms every level is completable and every mechanic required, but not whether the difficulty ramp feels right).
Slide-animation timing constants (game/drift-maze.html's Math.max(120, path.length * 55)) are a first pass, not playtested for feel.
Consider Orbit Duel: Rival AI (Cycle 2's runner-up concept) for a future cycle -- still low-risk and directly answers the original Cycle 1 follow-up.
No cross-browser testing beyond the environment's pre-installed Chromium.
